_meta.indication: XTANDI is indicated for the treatment of patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who have previously received docetaxel.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial; patients randomized 2:1 to XTANDI 160 mg once daily or placebo.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) who had previously received docetaxel-based chemotherapy.
pivotal_trials.result: At the prespecified interim analysis (520 events), median overall survival 18.4 months with XTANDI vs 13.6 months with placebo; HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.53, 0.75); p < 0.0001.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥5%) include asthenia/fatigue (50.6% vs 44.4% placebo), back pain (26.4% vs 24.3%), arthralgia (20.5% vs 17.3%). Seizure occurred in 0.9% (7 of 800) of XTANDI patients vs none on placebo; patients experiencing seizure were permanently discontinued from therapy. Grade ≥3 reactions occurred in 47% of XTANDI patients vs 53% placebo.
target_moa: Enzalutamide is an androgen receptor inhibitor that competitively inhibits androgen binding to androgen receptors and inhibits androgen receptor nuclear translocation and interaction with DNA.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because outside expertise was not necessary.

basis.text: Application received a priority review with a PDUFA date of 11/22/12; approved before that date because of the survival benefit.

citations.quote: Because of the survival benefit described below, this NDA is being approved well before the priority review PDUPA date of 11/22/12.

summary.text: XTANDI (enzalutamide) received regular (full) approval for mCRPC previously treated with docetaxel, based on a statistically significant overall survival benefit in the randomized Phase 3 CRPC2 trial. The NDA was granted priority review (PDUFA 11/22/12) and approved on a first cycle; no advisory committee was convened.

citations.quote: The clinical reviewers recommend regular approval of NDA 203415 that provides for the use of enzalutamide for “the treatment of patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) who have previously received docetaxel”.
Because of the survival benefit described below, this NDA is being approved well before the priority review PDUPA date of 11/22/12.
The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because outside expertise was not necessary; there were no controversial issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion.

requirement.text: 1918-1: Perform an in vitro screen to determine if N-desmethyl enzalutamide is metabolized by the major human CYP450 isozymes.

citations.quote: **1918-1:** Perform an in vitro screen to determine if N-desmethyl enzalutamide is metabolized by the major human CYP450 isozymes. Based on results from the in vitro screen, clinical drug-drug interaction trials may be needed.

requirement.text: 1918-2: Convene an expert panel and conduct a single-arm safety trial to assess the risk of seizure with enzalutamide 160 mg/day in at least 350 mCRPC patients at increased risk for seizure.

citations.quote: Following the panel's recommendations, conduct a single-arm safety trial to assess the risk of seizure with enzalutamide 160 mg/day in at least 350 patients with metastatic castrate-resistant prostate cancer who are at increased risk for seizure

requirement.text: 1918-3: Conduct a clinical trial in patients with normal hepatic function and pre-existing severe hepatic impairment to assess the effect of severe hepatic impairment on the PK of enzalutamide and N-desmethyl enzalutamide.

citations.quote: **1918-3:** Conduct a clinical trial in patients with normal hepatic function and patients with pre-existing severe hepatic impairment to assess the effect of severe hepatic impairment on the pharmacokinetics of enzalutamide and N-desmethyl enzalutamide. The proposed protocol must be submitted for review prior to trial initiation.

requirement.text: 1918-4: Conduct a drug interaction trial to evaluate the effect of rifampin (a strong CYP3A inducer and a moderate CYP2C8 inducer) on the PK of enzalutamide and N-desmethyl enzalutamide.
